The '''Caspian Pipeline Consortium''' ('''CPC''') is a consortium and an [[oil pipeline]] that transports Caspian oil from the [[Tengiz Field|Tengiz oil field]] in [[Kazakhstan]] to the [[Novorossiysk]]-2 Marine Terminal, an export terminal at the [[Russia]]n [[Black Sea]] [[port of Novorossiysk]].<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension>{{cite news|title=Russian court lifts suspension for Caspian pipeline operations|date=11 July 2022 |publisher=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/caspian-pipeline-fined-russia-suspension-lifted-2022-07-11/|accessdate=11 July 2022}}</ref> It is one of the world's largest pipelines<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension /> and a major export route for oil from the [[Kashagan Field|Kashagan]] and [[Karachaganak Field|Karachaganak]] fields.
The CPC pipeline transfers about 1% of [[global oil supply]]<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension /> and handles almost all of Kazakhstan's oil exports.<ref name=ReutersJuly11Analysis>{{cite news|last1=Valle|first1=Sabrina|last2=Bousso|first2=Ron|title=Analysis: Oil majors face output slump, deep losses if Russia stops Kazakh pipeline|date=11 July 2022|publisher=[[Reuters]]|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-majors-face-output-slump-deep-losses-if-russia-stops-kazakh-pipeline-2022-07-11/|accessdate=11 July 2022}}</ref> In 2021, the pipeline exported up to 1.3 million [[barrels per day]] (bpd)<ref name=ReutersJuly11Analysis /> of Kazakhstan's [[List of crude oil products|main crude grade]], [[Light crude oil|light]] [[Sour crude oil|sour]] CPC Blend, which represented 80% of Kazakhstan's total oil production of 1.6 million bpd.

The pipeline's largest shareholders include [[Chevron Corporation|Chevron]] and [[Exxon]].<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension />
{{As of|2009}}, the CPC pipeline was the only oil export pipeline in Russian territory not wholly owned by [[Transneft]].<ref name=ifri>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Dellecker|title=Caspian Pipeline Consortium, Bellwether of Russia's Investment Climate? Russie.Nei.visions no.31|date=June 2008|publisher=IFRI|url=http://www.ifri.org/files/Russie/ifri_RNV_Dellecker_CPC_ENG_juin2008.pdf|accessdate=2008-07-07|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081207213449/http://www.ifri.org/files/Russie/ifri_RNV_Dellecker_CPC_ENG_juin2008.pdf|archivedate=2008-12-07}}</ref>

== History ==
CPC was initially created in 1992 as a development by the Russian, Kazakhstani and [[Oman]]i governments to build a dedicated pipeline from [[Kazakhstan]] to export routes in the [[Black Sea]]. [[Chevron Corporation]] was asked to join, however talks broke down due to the high financial burden Chevron would have to take on relative to equity in the pipeline. Progress on the project stalled for several years until 1996 when a restructure included eight production companies in the project. Among the companies were Chevron, [[ExxonMobil|Mobil]], [[LUKoil]], [[Royal Dutch Shell]] and [[Rosneft]]. [[BP]] joined the consortium in 2003. Shares were divided fifty–fifty between the three states and the eight companies. Production companies financed the construction cost of US$2.67 billion, while the Russian Federation contributed unused pipeline assets worth US$293 million.<ref name=ifri /><ref name=cpc>{{cite web |title=Caspian Pipeline Consortium — a new global energy supplier|publisher=Caspian Pipeline Consortium |url=http://www.cpc.ru/_press/documents/cpc_a4_0303_en.pdf|accessdate=2008-11-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070809203256/http://www.cpc.ru/_press/documents/cpc_a4_0303_en.pdf |archivedate=2007-08-09}}</ref>

In April 2007, the Russian government transferred its shares to the Russian state-owned oil pipeline company [[Transneft]].<ref name=upstream1>{{cite news |title=Transneft takes CPC bite|date=2007-04-29|newspaper=[[Upstream (newspaper)|Upstream Online]]|publisher=NHST Media Group|url=http://www.upstreamonline.com/incoming/article132389.ece|accessdate=2008-07-07}}</ref> In October 2008, the Government of [[Oman]] sold its 7% stake to Transneft at a price of $700 million and withdrew from the project.<ref name=upstream2>{{cite news|title=Russia snaps up Oman CPC stake|date=2008-11-06|newspaper=[[Upstream (newspaper)|Upstream Online]]|publisher=NHST Media Group |url=http://www.upstreamonline.com/live/article166026.ece|accessdate=2008-11-09}}</ref> On 17 December 2008, a memorandum on expanding the pipeline was signed.<ref name=downstream171208>{{cite news|date=2008-12-17|title=CPC Shareholders Sign Expansion Deal|publisher=Downstream Today|url=http://www.downstreamtoday.com/News/Articles/200812/CPC_Shareholders_Sign_Expansion_Deal_14288.aspx|accessdate=2008-12-25}}</ref>

On October 14, 2016, crude oil from the [[Kashagan Field]] in Kazakhstan first started flowing into the Caspian Pipeline Consortium's system.<ref>{{Cite web |title=First Kashagan Oil is in CPC Pipeline System |url=http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2016/Pages/20161017.aspx |website=CPC}}</ref>

On April 18, 2018, the last pump station of CPC Expansion Project, PS-2 in [[Kalmykia]], was put into permanent operation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Last CPC Expansion Project Facility Commissioned in Kalmykia |url=http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2018/Pages/20180418_2.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180423165510/http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2018/Pages/20180418_2.aspx |archive-date=2018-04-23 |website=CPC |access-date=2020-08-03 }}</ref>

On May 21, 2019, the annual meeting of CPC shareholders adopted the Bottleneck Elimination Program (BEP), which provides for expansion of the [[Tengiz Field|Tengiz]]–[[Novorossiysk]] oil pipeline capacity to at least 72.5 million tons per year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Annual Meeting of CPC Corporate Governance Bodies|url=http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2019/Pages/20190522.aspx|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526050759/http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2019/Pages/20190522.aspx|archive-date=2019-05-26|website=CPC|access-date=2020-08-03}}</ref>

== Technical features ==
The diameter of the {{convert|1510|km|mi}} long oil pipeline varies between {{convert|1016|mm|in}} and {{convert|1067|mm|in}}. There are five pumping stations. The marine terminal includes two [[single buoy mooring|single point moorings]] and the tank farm consists of four steel storage tanks of {{convert|100000|m3}} each. Pipeline throughflow started at {{convert|350000|oilbbl/d}} and has since increased to {{convert|700000|oilbbl/d}}.<ref name=cpc /><ref name=cpc2>{{cite web|title=CPC Project Basic Features|publisher=Caspian Pipeline Consortium|url=http://www.cpc.ru/portal/alias!press/lang!en-US/tabID!3444/DesktopDefault.aspx|accessdate=2008-11-22|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221050413/http://www.cpc.ru/portal/alias%21press/lang%21en-US/tabID%213444/DesktopDefault.aspx|archivedate=2008-12-21}}</ref>

The second stage reached a capacity of {{convert|1.4|Moilbbl/d|m3/d}}.<ref name=S&P010922>{{cite news|date=2022-01-09|title=Kazakhstan's Tengiz oil field operator says resuming normal output after protests|publisher=S&P Global Commodity Insights|url=https://www.spglobal.com/commodity-insights/en/market-insights/latest-news/oil/010922-kazakhstans-tengiz-oil-field-operator-says-resuming-normal-output-after-protests|accessdate=2022-03-23}}</ref> As of 2022, the pipeline throughput was about {{convert|1.2|Moilbbl/d|m3/d}}, about 1.2% of global oil demand.<ref name=reuters-20220322>{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/russia-warns-sharp-caspian-pipeline-oil-export-drop-after-storm-2022-03-22/|title=Russia warns of sharp Caspian pipeline oil export drop after storm|publisher=Reuters|url-access=subscription|date=22 March 2022|access-date=23 March 2022}}</ref>

== Operations ==
In 2008, CPC transported 31.5 million tons of crude, down from 32.6 million tonnes in 2007.  In the first three months of 2009, the pipeline transported 8.7 million tonnes of oil.<ref name=silkroad>{{cite news|title=CPC pipeline exports up in 2009|date=2009-04-06|publisher=Silk Road Intelligencer|url=http://silkroadintelligencer.com/2009/04/06/cpc-pipeline-exports-up-in-2009/|accessdate=2009-04-06|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811042435/http://silkroadintelligencer.com/2009/04/06/cpc-pipeline-exports-up-in-2009/|archivedate=2010-08-11}}</ref>

From 2001 to April 31, 2020, the [[Tengiz Field|Tengiz]]–[[Novorossiysk]] pipeline system carried 662,784,671 tons of net oil to world markets. Of this, 582,814,809 tons was from Kazakhstan and 85,295,642 tons was produced in Russia. The total number of tankers processed during this period was 6,287.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CPC Marine Terminal April shipments |url=http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2020/Pages/20200506.aspx |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200509112852/http://www.cpc.ru/EN/press/releases/2020/Pages/20200506.aspx |archive-date=2020-05-09 |website=CPC|access-date=2020-08-03}}</ref>

In March 2022, two of the three pipeline-connected ship berths at the [[Port of Novorossiysk]] suffered storm damage. Repairs were expected to take up to two months, with exports falling by up to 1 million barrels per day.<ref name=reuters-20220322 />

On 6 July 2022, a [[Judiciary of Russia|Russian court]] ordered the suspension of the pipeline for 30 days over [[oil spill]]s. The CPC appealed the ruling and the suspension was lifted on 11 July of the following week, and the CPC was fined 200,000 rubles (US$3,300).<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension /> Despite the July 6 ruling, the operator of Kazakhstan's [[Tengiz Field|Tengiz oil field]], [[Tengizchevroil]], said that the transfer of oil through the CPC had not been interrupted since immediate suspension of the pipeline was technically impossible and would have resulted in "irreversible consequences".<ref name=ReutersJuly11Suspension />

The CPC pipeline carries most of Kazakhstan's oil exports, which makes the country's oil supply routes heavily dependent on Russia. In addition, about 15% of the rest of Kazakhstan's oil exports are also transferred through Russia<ref name=ReutersJuly11Analysis /> (while about 5% is sent to China or to various other destinations over rail and the [[Caspian Sea]]<ref name=ReutersJuly11Analysis />). After the 6 July suspension of the pipeline, [[President of Kazakhstan|Kazakhstan's President]] [[Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] ordered the government of his country to diversify its oil supply routes.

In November 2024 the [[International Consortium of Investigative Journalists]] and 26 media partners published the report "Caspian Cabals" to put public interests on environmental damage, but also to allegations of financial corruption and geopolitical threats.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-22 |title=Putin’s pipeline: How the Kremlin outmaneuvered Western oil companies to wrest control of vast flows of Kazakhstan’s crude |url=https://www.icij.org/investigations/caspian-cabals/kazakhstan-caspian-oil-pipeline-russia-chevron/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=International Consortium of Investigative Journalists |language=en-US}}</ref>

As part of a new sanctions package against Russia imposed on 10 January 2025, the [[United States Department of the Treasury|U.S. Department of the Treasury]] granted exemptions for oilfield services related to the CPC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-10 |title=New U.S. sanctions against Russian energy interests |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/new-us-sanctions-against-russian-energy-interests-2025-01-10/ |website=Reuters}}</ref>

== Attacks ==
{{main article|Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)}}

On 17 February 2025, on the eve of talks between the U.S. and Russian officials on ending the war in [[Ukraine]], a drone attack by the [[Ukrainian Air Force]] on a pumping station damaged energy equipment, a gas turbine unit, and a substation. Flows through the CPC were reduced by 30–40%.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-02-18 |title=Russia says drone attack cut oil via Kazakhstan Caspian pipeline by up to 40% |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/russia-says-ukrainian-drone-attack-pipeline-carrying-1-global-crude-could-2025-02-18/ |access-date=2015-02-19 |website=Reuters}}</ref> The station was expected to be restored within one-and-a-half to two months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petroni |first=Giulia |date=2025-02-18 |title=Drone Attack on Caspian Pipeline Could Cut Oil Volumes From Kazakhstan by 30% |url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/drone-attack-on-caspian-pipeline-could-cut-oil-volumes-from-kazakhstan-by-30-2b62fdee |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=MarketWatch |language=EN-US}}</ref>

On November 29, one of the three mooring points on the CPC pier was damaged as a result of a maritime drone attack. CPC reported that no oil leaked into the Black Sea and that operations at the terminal were suspended.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Терминал КТК получил повреждения при атаке дронов|url=https://www.rbc.ru/politics/29/11/2025/692ab0179a794764233d12d2|website=РБК|date=2025-11-29|access-date=2025-11-29|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/cpc-says-oil-exports-halted-equipment-heavily-damaged-by-drones-2025-11-29/|title=CPC says oil exports halted, equipment heavily damaged by drones|date=2025-11-29|access-date=2025-11-29|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> In connection with the incident, the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Kazakhstan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan]] expressed a protest, stating that it was "already the third act of aggression" against an "exclusively civilian object" and that such actions damage Kazakhstan's bilateral relations with Ukraine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Казахстан предупредил об ущербе отношениям с Украиной из-за атаки на КТК|url=https://www.rbc.ru/rbcfreenews/692bba369a7947266846c919|website=РБК|date=2025-11-30|access-date=2025-11-30|language=ru}}</ref> [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine|Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry]] essentially acknowledged responsibility for the strikes on the CPC terminal, rebuked Kazakhstan for what it sees as an insufficiently firm stance toward Russia, and signaled that it considers collateral damage on Russian territory to be quite acceptable.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Сопутствующий ущерб. К чему приведут удары по нефтепроводу из Казахстана |url=https://carnegieendowment.org/russia-eurasia/politika/2025/12/russia-caspian-oil-strike?lang=ru |access-date=2025-12-05 |website=Carnegie Endowment for International Peace |language=ru}}</ref> However, according to the [[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace|Carnegie Berlin Center]], these attacks inflict relatively limited economic damage on Russia while threatening tens of billions in revenue for Kazakhstan and Western oil companies, thereby alienating important Ukrainian partners and provoking political backlash among its allies.<ref name=":0" />

On 17 July 2026 at 07:00 a.m. [[Moscow Time|MSK]], the Nordic American tankers vessel ''Nordic Zenith'', chartered by [[ExxonMobil]], was damaged by two drone strikes and caught fire as it approached the [[Port of Novorossiysk]] and the CPC terminal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-18 |title=Exxon-chartered oil tanker attacked by drones near Black Sea terminal |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chartered-oil-tanker-attacked-by-drones-near-black-sea-terminal-cpc-says-2026-07-17/ |website=Reuters}}</ref> On the same day, the [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine|Ukraine Unmanned Systems Forces]] published a strike map with the location of ''Nordic Zenith'' indicated as part of [[Operation MoLoChKa]], a campaign against vessels of the [[Russian shadow fleet]], despite the vessel being a neutral, Western-owned ship in compliance with international sanctions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-17 |title=Unmanned Systems Forces hit 12 more ships of russian "shadow fleet" in Black Sea {{!}} Ukrainian news |url=https://ukranews.com/en/news/1163646-unmanned-systems-forces-hit-12-more-ships-of-russian-shadow-fleet-in-black-sea |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=ukranews.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Junnola |first=Jill |date=2026-07-17 |title=CPC Suffers Tanker Strike, Single Point Mooring Delay |url=https://www.energyintel.com/0000019f-7045-d11d-afff-f5efeaa30000 |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=Energy Intelligence |language=en}}</ref>

==Consortium==
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium was initially registered in the [[Bermuda]] Islands in 1992.<ref name=ifri /> It is split into two companies: CPC-R operates the Russian section of the pipeline and CPC-K operates the Kazakh section.<ref name=ifri />

The shareholders of the consortium are:

* [[Transneft]] – 24%
* [[KazMunayGas|KazMunaiGaz]] – 19%
* [[Chevron Corporation|Chevron]] Caspian Pipeline Consortium Co. – 15%
* [[LukArco]] B.V. – 12.5%
* [[Mobil]] Caspian Pipeline Co. – 7.5%
* [[Rosneft]] – Shell Caspian Ventures Ltd. – 7.5%
* CPC Company – 7%
* [[BG Group|BG Overseas Holdings Ltd.]] – 2%
* [[Eni]] International (N.A.) N.V. S.ar.l – 2%
* Kazakhstan Pipeline Ventures LLC – 1.75%
* Oryx Caspian Pipeline LLC<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORYX CASPIAN PIPELINE L.L.C – CompaniesRegistry.cy |url=https://companiesregistry.cy/company-details/oryx-caspian-pipeline-l-l-c-2137/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Companies Registry Cyprus |language=en-US}}</ref> – 1.75%

extract:
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) is a consortium and an oil pipeline that transports Caspian oil from the Tengiz oil field in Kazakhstan to the Novorossiysk-2 Marine Terminal, an export terminal at the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk. It is one of the world's largest pipelines and a major export route for oil from the Kashagan and Karachaganak fields.
The CPC pipeline transfers about 1% of global oil supply and handles almost all of Kazakhstan's oil exports. In 2021, the pipeline exported up to 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) of Kazakhstan's main crude grade, light sour CPC Blend, which represented 80% of Kazakhstan's total oil production of 1.6 million bpd.
The pipeline's largest shareholders include Chevron and Exxon.
As of 2009, the CPC pipeline was the only oil export pipeline in Russian territory not wholly owned by Transneft.
